name: Abercrombie & Fitch Bug Bounty
policy:
Abercrombie & Fitch Management Co. (ANF) looks forward to working with the security community to find vulnerabilities in order to keep our businesses and customers safe.

# Safe Harbor

Any activities conducted in a manner consistent with this policy will be considered authorized conduct and we will not initiate legal action against you. If legal action is initiated by a third party against you in connection with activities conducted consistently with this policy, we will take steps to make it known that your actions were authorized.

# Disclosure Policy

-   As this is a private program, please do not discuss this program or any vulnerabilities (even resolved ones) outside of the program without express written consent from Abercrombie & Fitch Management Co.
-   Follow HackerOne's [disclosure guidelines](https://www.hackerone.com/disclosure-guidelines).

# Program Rules

Please provide detailed reports with reproducible steps. If the report is not detailed enough to reproduce the issue, the issue will not be eligible for a reward.

- We are continuously scanning our applications for vulnerabilities. Abercrombie & Fitch will operate in good faith to pay out net new vulnerabilities disclosed through this program. Findings related to newly released CVEs will be evaluated against Abercrombie & Fitch’s existing vulnerability management processes. Cases in which the vulnerability has already been triaged and slated for remediation within SLAs will be treated as a duplicate findings. 
-   Submit one vulnerability per report, unless you need to chain vulnerabilities to provide impact. Multiple vulnerabilities caused by one underlying issue will be awarded one bounty.
-   When duplicates occur, we only award the first report that was received (provided that it can be fully reproduced).
- If using a publicly available POC / exploit, please provide the source. This helps ANF understand risk, impact and remediate. Leveraging public POCs will not result in reduced bounty. Providing sources of lesser-known successful exploits may result in a bonus reward. 
-   Exfiltration and/or exposure of personally identifiable information is expressly prohibited. If you believe a vulnerability exists where PII may be exposed, please ensure you are using your own test accounts for POC.
- If submitting a ticket regarding found system credentials, researchers must provide the source. Credentials must not be used to access underlying systems. Tickets will be evaluated and assigned a value at ANF's discretion based on the class of identity and its level of access.
-   Social engineering (e.g. phishing, vishing, smishing) including interactions with customer service or chat agents is prohibited.
-   Make a good faith effort to avoid privacy violations, destruction of data, and interruption or degradation of our service. Only interact with accounts you own.
- A&F corporate employees, contractors (past and current), and connected entities are not eligible for participation in this program.
- Abercrombie’s and Hollister Co.’s underlying architecture is the same. The same rule can be applied to exposed non-prod environments if found. Refrain from submitting a duplicate report for the other domain or environment. 

# Test Plan

-   We strongly recommend the use of a modified a user agent in your HTTP(S) requests, and for non-HTTP requests we strongly recommend you add an identification to artifacts in POCs, and, or payloads so our teams can identify you as a verified researcher and not a malicious attacker: (e.g. h1:`<bbp-hackeroneusername>`).
-   No credentials are required or provided for this program. If you self-register for any accounts, please register with your [@wearehackerone](https://hackerone.com/wearehackerone).com email address. You may not use exposed credentials to continue testing without explicit written approval of Abercrombie & Fitch Management Co.

# Out of scope vulnerabilities

### When reporting vulnerabilities, please consider (1) attack scenario / exploitability, and (2) security impact of the bug. The following issues are considered out of scope:

-   Clickjacking on pages with no sensitive actions
-   Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on unauthenticated forms or forms with no sensitive actions
-   Attacks requiring MITM or physical access to a user's device.
-   Previously known vulnerable libraries without a working Proof of Concept.
-   Comma Separated Values (CSV) injection without demonstrating a vulnerability.
-   Missing best practices in SSL/TLS configuration.
-   Any activity that could lead to the disruption of our service (DoS).
-   Content spoofing and text injection issues without showing an attack vector/without being able to modify HTML/CSS
-   Rate limiting, bruteforce or enumeration issues on non-authentication endpoints
-   Missing best practices in Content Security Policy.
-   Missing email best practices (Invalid, incomplete or missing SPF/DKIM/DMARC records, etc.)
-   Vulnerabilities only affecting users of outdated or unpatched browsers [Less than 2 stable versions behind the latest released stable version]
-   Software version disclosure / Banner identification issues / Descriptive error messages or headers (e.g. stack traces, application or server errors) without PoC are considered informational.
-   Public Zero-day vulnerabilities that have had an official patch for less than 1 month will be awarded on a case by case basis.
-   Tabnabbing and typosquatting
-   Open redirect - unless an additional security impact can be demonstrated
-   Issues that require unlikely user interaction, including but not limited to phishing.
-   Promotional code abuse
-   Social Engineering of customer service agents via voice or chat

# Response Targets

Abercrombie & Fitch Management Co. will make a best effort to meet the following SLAs for hackers participating in our program:

**SLA in business days**

| Type of Response | SLA in business days |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| First Response | 2 days |
| Time to Triage | 2 days |
| Time to Bounty | 14 days |
| Time to Resolution | depends on severity and complexity |

We’ll try to keep you informed about our progress throughout the process.

Thank you for helping keep Abercrombie & Fitch Management Co. and our users safe!
